rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says idh denotes the nearest knowledge here; if it means power alone, it is best construed as competing with naʿlamu for governance.
rows.anchor: bu اِذْ’de akreb ilim mânasında, yalnız kudret mânasında ise نَعْلَمُ ile tenâzu‘üzere âmil olmak yaraşır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two angels are assigned to each person, seated on the right and left, recording every utterance, good or evil, without missing anything.
rows.anchor: her insanın söylediğini telakkī ile zabta me’mur iki melek vardır, ifadesini zabteder dururlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is nearer to a person than the angels and knows hidden matters in the soul that even they cannot perceive, with power to act as He wills.
rows.anchor: Allah ona her yakından daha yakındır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ recording and preservation serves human beings’ future reckoning; God has no need of their records.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde o meleklerin zabt u hıfzı O’nun ihtiyâcından değil kulların istikbâli için hikmete mebnîdir

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf cites a report from the Prophet: the angels sit by the front teeth, the tongue is their pen and saliva their ink, while people chatter without shame before God or them.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf’ta der ki: “Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den şöyle mervîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s apparent sense is that the angels write every word spoken; its indication also implies that they record deeds.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetin zâhirinden anlaşıldığına göre bu melekler ağızdan çıkan her sözü yazarlar, bunun delâletinden ef‘âli de yazdıkları anlaşılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context indicates that God knows inward whispers that remain hidden from the recording angels.
rows.anchor: Mâkabline nazaran sevkinden de nefisteki vesveseler gibi bazı şeylerin Allah’a mâlum olmakla beraber onlardan gizli kaldığı anlaşılmıştı

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Imam Malik is reported to say that everything is written, even a person's groan while ill.
rows.anchor: İmâm Mâlik “her şey yazılır, hattâ hastalıktaki enîni bile” demiştir

rows.speaker: لقّاني
rows.claim: Al-Lakkani, as quoted by al-Alusi from Jawhara and its commentary, says angels write all good and evil deeds, words, beliefs, intentions, resolutions, and decisions, whether deliberate or forgetful, in health or illness.
rows.anchor: Cevhere ve şerhi Lakkānî’de Âlûsî’nin nakline göre şöyle denilmiştir[^3]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Passing inner thoughts that never reach intention, resolve, or decision are not written; these are unsettled self-whispers.
rows.anchor: Demek ki hemm, azim, karar mertebelerine gelmeyen vesveseler yazılmaz, bu cihetle مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ hemm ve kasd mertebesine gelmeyen ehâdîs-i nefs

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits from Hudhayfa that speech has seven locks and is not written until it passes through them: heart, uvula, tongue, jaws, and lips.
rows.anchor: Beyhakī Şu‘ab’da Huzeyfe b. el-Yemân radıyallâhu anh’tan şöyle tahric etmiştir: “Kelâmın yedi kilidi vardır

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some hold that permissible idle speech is not recorded; only words carrying reward, punishment, or responsibility are recorded.
rows.anchor: bazıları mubâhâtın yazılmadığına, ancak sevab veya ikābı bulunanların yani mes’ûliyeti olanların yazıldığına kāil olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı holds that every outward act and utterance is written, while some inward matters are not; what reaches memory, however, counts as written.
rows.anchor: Biz zâhire çıkan her fi‘l ü kavlin yazıldığına, bâtında kalanlardan yazılmayanlar bulunduğuna, ma‘amâfîh hafızaya geçenlerin yazılmış demek olduğuna kāiliz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is pictured not as someone whose biography is written in absentia, but as a suspect questioned in person or a dying patient watched at bedside, inwardly stirred by fear and hope.
rows.anchor: insan, gıyâbında terceme-i hâli yazılan bir şahıs vaziyetinde değil, ya müstantık huzûrunda ifadesi zabtolunan ve gönlünden heyecanlar ve vesveseler geçen bir müttehem

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This portrayal leads from the angels' surveillance to death and the afterlife; even at death God is nearer than the jugular, as 56:85 says.
rows.anchor: Bu nükte iledir ki buradan mevt ve âhirete geçilerek buyuruluyor ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The agony of death is its intense severity that takes away the mind.
rows.anchor: Mevtin sekresi, sekerâtı aklı gideren şiddetidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death comes with truth when God's command brings the reality that every soul must taste death.
rows.anchor: ölümün hak ile gelmesi Allah’ın emriyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indicated event is the second blowing of the trumpet and the Day of Warning, when the warning is fulfilled and recompense is given.
rows.anchor: yani va‘îdin incaz edileceği, cezâ verileceği gün

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul reaches the gathering accompanied by two kinds of angels: one assigned to drive it there and another to witness its deeds.
rows.anchor: İki nevi melek birisi o nefsi mahşere sevke me’mur, birisi de ameline şâhid

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness most readily understood is one of the guardian angels who monitored the person.
rows.anchor: Şâhidin murakabe eden hafaza melâikesinden olması tebâdür eder

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify the driver as the angel recording evil deeds and the witness as the angel recording good deeds; other explanations are also reported, and God knows best.
rows.anchor: Bazıları seyyiâtı yazan sâik, hasenâtı yazan şâhid demişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement may stand independently or serve as the predicate of an omitted saying.
rows.anchor: Bu cümle ya istinâfiye[^9] veya mukadder kavlin mekūlüdür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address applies to everyone because all people have some heedlessness of the afterlife, and hearing about it is not like seeing it.
rows.anchor: Hepsine bu hitâbın yapılması herkeste âhiretten az çok bir gaflet bulunması, ليس الخبر كالعيان olması hikmetine mebnîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion who says this is the attendant driver who brings the person before God.
rows.anchor: Ve karîni demiştir yani yanındaki sâik Hak teâlâ’nın huzûruna ihzar edip böyle demiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion in this exchange is Satan, who had overpowered the unbeliever in worldly life and accompanies him to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Bu karîn, dünyada o kâfire musallat olup âhirette beraber sevkolunan Şeytan olduğu şu sözünden bellidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's defense answers the person's attempted excuse and complaint that Satan made him transgress.
rows.anchor: Demek oluyor ki “yâ Rab[^10], beni bu azıttı” diye i‘tizar ve şikayet etmek istemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan says the person was already far from the truth, so he merely approached him, echoing 14:22 that Satan only called people and had no authority over them.
rows.anchor: Yani kendisi haktan uzağa sapmış bulunuyordu da ben ona öyle yanaştım وَمَا كَانَ لِىَ عَلَيْكُم مِّن سُلْطَٰنٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forbids the disputants to quarrel in His presence and says He had already warned them through scriptures and prophets while they still had time to act.
rows.anchor: mukaddemâ dünyada çalışma çağında kitaplarla ve peygamberlerle inzar etmiş, tuğyan edenlere böyle şiddetli azab edileceğini haber vererek tenbihler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's word is not changed: neither promise nor warning is altered; forgiving some sinners applies evidence that qualifies the warning, rather than changing it.
rows.anchor: Benim nezdimde söz değiştirilmez vaad değiştirilmediği gibi va‘îd de değiştirilmez. Bazı günahkârlardan af meselesi ise tebdil değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's declaration of not wronging His servants confirms the universal principle that the warning's fulfillment is the consequence of their own desert.
rows.anchor: va‘îdin tatbîki kendi istihkaklarının neticesi olduğunu tefhimdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Tūr is Mount Sinai, where Moses heard God's speech.
rows.anchor: Kasem olsun o Tûr’a Hazret-i Mûsâ’nın

rows.speaker: بيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi says Tūr means mountain in Syriac; he also offers an alternative description linking it to the passage from the unseen realm to the visible realm.
rows.anchor: Beyzâvî der ki: “Tûr, Süryânîde dağ demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rakk is thin leather prepared for writing and, by extension, can mean any writing surface; manshur is opened and spread rather than rolled or closed, while mastur is orderly writing.
rows.anchor: “Rakk” kâğıt hâline getirilmiş yazı yazılan ince deri demektir. O münasebetle “varak” gibi, yazı yazılan her şeye de ıtlak olunabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manshur means unrolled, opened, and spread; mastur describes something written in an orderly arrangement.
rows.anchor: neşredilmiş, dürülü, kapalı değil, açılmış, yayılmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the phrase uses an indefinite book rather than al-kitab, Elmalılı favors the book of deeds, a new book unknown beforehand, as in 17:13; the Preserved Tablet or Quran remain possible.
rows.anchor: nekre olarak وَكِتَٰبٍۢ مَّسْطُورٍۢ buyurulması, bunun henüz tanınmadık başka bir kitap olduğunu andırır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book may alternatively be the Preserved Tablet or, as a newly revealed book, the Quran.
rows.anchor: Levh-i Mahfuz veya yeni bir kitap olmak itibariyle Kur’an olması da melhuzdur

rows.speaker: رواية
rows.claim: One report identifies Bayt al-Maʿmur as a house in the seventh heaven visited daily by seventy thousand angels, each of whom does not return, and also calls it Durah.
rows.anchor: bir rivayete göre yedinci semâda bir beyttir ki, her gün onu yetmiş bin melâike ziyaret eder

rows.speaker: حسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri reportedly identifies Bayt al-Maʿmur as the Kaaba, which God fills each year with six hundred thousand people, adding angels if the human visitors are fewer.
rows.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî’den bir rivayette de murad Kâbe’dir. Allah teâlâ onu her sene altı yüz bin kişi ile ma‘mur kılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A place being maʿmur figuratively means it is inhabited, frequented, and well tended; the Kaaba is made prosperous by visitors and pilgrims, as in 22:26 and 2:125.
rows.anchor: Mâlum ki bir yerin ma‘mur olması demek meskun olması ve geleni gideni çok olup güzel bakılması mânasından mecazdır

rows.speaker: بيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi also suggests that Bayt al-Maʿmur is the believer's heart, made prosperous through knowledge of God and sincerity.
rows.anchor: Beyzâvî der ki: “Yahut Beyt-i Ma‘mûr’dan murad mü’minin kalbidir ki ma‘mûriyeti marifet ve ihlâs iledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised roof is the sky; another report takes it to be the Throne, the roof of Paradise.
rows.anchor: ve sakf-ı merfû‘a o yüksek tavana, yani semâya, bir rivayette de cennetin sakfı olan Arş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masjur can mean kindled or heated: at the Resurrection the seas will become fire and boil, heating Hell, as 81:6 says.
rows.anchor: Alevlendirilmiş, kızdırılmış demektir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masjur may mean full or overflowing, expressing the all-encompassing ocean.
rows.anchor: 2. Dolgun, taşkın demek olup bahr-ı muhît mânasını ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masjur may also describe mixed waters, with fresh and salty water mixing together.
rows.anchor: 3. Muhtelit, karışkan, suyu birbirine veya tatlısı acısına karışan demek de olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As one of the words with opposite senses, masjur is also said to mean empty, which would make the sea a sign of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: 4. Ezdâddan olarak boş mânasına geldiği de söylenmiştir ki bu da kıyamet alâmetlerinden demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the mention of Tūr, the sea may also allude to the sea in which Pharaoh drowned.
rows.anchor: Tûr karînesiyle bu “bahr-ı mescûr” Firavun’un battığı denize işaret olmak da pek melhuzdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first wa is the oath particle, and the following oath subjects are coordinated with it.
rows.anchor: Başta vâv kasem, sonrakiler ona atıf içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Lord's punishment will certainly occur is the answer to the oath.
rows.anchor: Kasemin cevâbıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is an adverb modifying la-waqiʿ; the sky's churning portrays the turmoil of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: لَوَٰقِعٌۭ’in zarfıdır, yani o gün vâki‘olacak ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains will move from their places and become scattered dust.
rows.anchor: Dağlar da bir yürüyüş yürüyecek yerinden oynayıp hebâen mensûrâ olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Woe is for deniers who play about in falsehood instead of believing, preparing for that day, and seeking protection.
rows.anchor: bir batakta oynarlar iman edip de o gün için hazırlanacak, korunacak yerde birtakım yalan dolana dalmış uğraşır dururlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are forcibly shoved toward Hellfire.
rows.anchor: Cehennem ateşine bir kakılış kakılacakları gün

words: يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا

rows.claim: This yawm either replaces the preceding yawm or is accusative under an implied saying, explaining the woe.

words: هَٰذِهِ ٱلنَّارُ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As they are shoved into the fire, they are told that this is the fire they used to deny.
rows.anchor: Yani o gün böyle diyerek kakılacaklar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in the question is coordinated with an implied preceding statement.
rows.anchor: fâ-i mukaddere ma‘tuftur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had called revelation's warning about the fire sorcery or deception; when it materializes, they are challenged whether this too is sorcery.
rows.anchor: siz bu ateşi haber veren vahye bir sihir, bir aldatma diyordunuz, şimdi onun böyle fiilen tahakkuku da sihir mi? ilh... Böyle denecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In wa-al-najm, the definite article may be anaphoric or generic.
rows.anchor: En-Necme kasem Lâm ahid de cins de olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najm may mean a star, a plant without a trunk such as grass, or each installment of something given in portions; each Quranic installment over its 23-year descent is called a najm.
rows.anchor: “Necm” birkaç mânaya gelir, burada her birine ihtimal verilmiştir. 1. Evvelâ mâlum olduğu üzere yıldız demektir. 2. Şecer mukabili olarak sâkı olmayan ot, çemen mânasına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najm can denote each portion of a thing delivered gradually; since the Quran descended over 23 years, each revealed portion is called a najm.
rows.anchor: Kur’an da yirmi üç senede ceste ceste nâzil olduğundan müneccemen nâzil oldu denilir ve her defasında nâzil olan miktarına bir necm ıtlak edilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With anaphoric al, najm became a proper name for the Pleiades, a prominent star cluster resembling a bunch of grapes and the third lunar mansion.
rows.anchor: lâm-ı ahd ayrılmamak şartıyla وَٱلنَّجْمِ bilhassa Süreyya’ya yani Ülker yıldızına isim olmuştur ki esmâ-i gālibe kabîlindendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arab proverb says that when the Pleiades rises in the evening, the shepherd seeks a garment, since its rising coincides with sunset and the season's cold.
rows.anchor: Araplar mesel olarak إذَا طَلَعَ الن َّجْمُ عِشَاءً اِبـْتـَغَى ال َّراعِي كِسَاءً “Ülker akşam doğarsa çoban örtü ister” derler

rows.speaker: حديث
rows.claim: A hadith is cited saying that when the Pleiades rises in the morning, the blight or pestilence lifts.
rows.anchor: bir hadiste de إذَا طَلَعَ الن َّجْمُ صَبَاحًا اِرْتـَفَعَتِ الْعَاهَةُ vârid olmuştur ki “Ülker sabahleyin doğarsa âfet kalkar”

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators identify the oath's najm as the Pleiades because it is the most conspicuous star and the best-known lunar mansion; they take huwwiyy as rising.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle Süreyya yıldızın en göze çarpanı ve menâzilin en meşhuru olmak hasebiyle burada müfessirlerin bazıları bununla tefsir etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Because Sirius is mentioned later in the surah, some identify najm as Sirius, also taking huwwiyy to mean rising.
rows.anchor: bu sûrede رَبُّ ٱلشِّعْرَىٰ geleceği cihetle bazıları da burada lâm-ı ahd ile “en-Necm” Şi‘râ yıldızı olduğunu söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many interpreters take al-najm generically to mean stars generally, considering its sense either literal or figurative.
rows.anchor: Birçokları da lâm-ı cins ile mutlak yıldız mânasına haml eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq says the intended referent is the Prophet; on this reading huwwiyy means his descent from the Miʿraj or ascent into the placeless realm.
rows.anchor: Ca‘fer-i Sâdık Hazretleri “murad Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’dir”

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الفراء، منذر بن سعيد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Farra, and Qadi Mundhir ibn Saʿid say najm refers to the portion of the Quran that descends.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas, Mücâhid, Ferrâ ve Kâdî Münzir b. Sa‘îd burada “en-Necm”den murad Kur’ân’ın nüzul eden miktarı demek olduğunu söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: نيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi says that reading makes the oath comparable to the oath by the Wise Quran in 36:2–3.
rows.anchor: Nîsâbûrî der ki: “Bu surette

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers najm to mean the descending portion of the Quran and leaves it untranslated in Turkish so the other possibilities remain available.
rows.anchor: Biz de bu mânayı tercih etmek istiyoruz. Bunun için mealde “necm”i “yıldız” diye tercüme etmeyip bu ihtimallere muntabık olabilmek üzere şöyle diyoruz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawa-yahwi can mean to glide down swiftly like a hawk, descend, fall, or shoot upward; stars' setting or rising can be described as their movement toward or from the horizon.
rows.anchor: şahinin inişi gibi sür‘atle süzülüp inmek ve düşmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the fourth verbal form hawa-yahwa, the noun hawa means desire, inclination to appetite, or infatuation.
rows.anchor: Bu madde dördüncü babdan olarak هَوِيَ - يـَهْوَى diye kullanıldığı zaman da masdarı هَوًى gelir ki nefsin şehvetine meyli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The celestial bodies swim in their orbits, as 36:40 says; Elmalılı presents gravitation as a law of falling.
rows.anchor: hepsi sukūt kanununa tâbi‘dirler. Gravitation kanunu bir heveyân kanunudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If najm means stars, huwwiyy may be rising or setting; travelers navigate by these moments, and the setting of stars generally marks dawn, making the oath an oath by morning.
rows.anchor: yıldızların tulû‘veya gurûb lahzalarıyla istidlâl ederek yol bulurlar. Umum yıldızların gurûbu ise sabah vakti demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If najm means grass, its huwwiyy is the time when plants rise and bend down, the height of spring.
rows.anchor: Çemen mânasında ise “heveyân” otların yükselip yere yattığı zamandır ki baharın kuvvetli çağıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If najm is the Quran, its descent is the moment of each revelation; the oath by the moment of revelation confirms the following assertion with emphasis.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın necmi olduğuna göre ise “hüviy” onun nüzûlü demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dalal is the opposite of guidance: losing one's way or being unable to find a way; ghayy is the opposite of right-mindedness, losing sound judgment or the straight road.
rows.anchor: “Gayy” da “rüşd”ün zıddı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion is Muhammad, and the address is directed to Quraysh and their like, who accused him of inventing the Quran.
rows.anchor: “Sâhib”den murad, Muhammed Mustafa sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’dir. Hitab da ona “Kur’ân’ı kendi uyduruyor” diyen Kureyş ve eşbâhınadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him their companion stresses that they know him from close association as sound-minded, and that he is their friend and protector seeking to guide them; he neither goes astray nor loses his mind, deceives, nor is deceived.
rows.anchor: sâhib dâima sohbette bulunan arkadaş ve sahâbet edip koruyan hâmî mânalarını ifade ettiği için şu meâli ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His speech, especially his recitation of the Quran, does not arise from personal opinion, desire, or inclination; he is neither a poet nor one who rules by whim.
rows.anchor: onun nutku bâhusus Kur’ân’ı nâtık olması kendisinin re’y ü arzusundan, gönlünün meyl ü sevdâsından neş’et etmez. Öyle sırf nefsî bir söyleyiş değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in in huwa may refer either to the Quran or to the Prophet's speech.
rows.anchor: O yani Kur’an veya onun nutku

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran or this speech is revelation alone, known and spoken through God's revelation and communication; knowledge of truths, especially future events, depends on divine disclosure.
rows.anchor: yalnız {يُوحَىٰ} vahyolunur Allah teâlâ tarafından
